title: Choosing Greenwald School of Music on the GI Bill
summary: After considering the Navy and barber college he enrolled at Greenwald, taught by college faculty; alumni include Red Tyler and Earl Palmer.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: I would sing, you know. But, um, and musically, I would think of that. First of all, first of all, first of all, first I started to go to, uh, I would sing, you know.

And, uh, I would sing, you know. But, um, and musically, I would think of what I wanted to do. Um, I had this singing thing was always in the back of my mind. I would sing, you know. But, um, and musically, I would think, first of all, first I started to go to, first I started to go back in the service, okay, I threw that out. That stayed in my mind a long time. Then I decided, I'm going to go to Barber College. I won't be no Barber. So, and then when I started singing, I said, well, I'm going to go to music school. And Greenwald School of Music opened for GIs. And of all of the music schools, and this was a better music school than the colleges were offered. Because we had all of the college people teaching. Our professor, the man who was in charge of our school was a professor from Dillard University. Well, anyway, he left here and went back. But he was, see, because they had quite a few people. And we had all of the music instructors from Xavier, Dillard, and all the other private instructors who were real good. And we had a heck of a school with them. Now, most of your better musicians in the city today, like Red Tyler, Earl Palmer, Ernest McLean, all of the people who really wound up being musicians in the top, they came from Greenwald.
That's that. So once you got into Greenwald, what was your day like? What was your instruction like?

Oh, well, they were, they were, we had, you know, like I said, the instructions were real professional, and we were taught music on a college level, you know. So you had to learn something. We had, in fact, I still had some projects from my Greenwald School. And it was things, that's, I think, that's why, I think, that's why, I had to learn something. In fact, I had to learn something. I had a better foundation than a lot of the younger musicians today. Because the things that we know about, they don't know about it today. Now, there are some things that they have a more advanced training in some things musically. But it don't take up the five minutes to get it. Right. So, you know, I don't know about the things that we did. Not at all.
